title: Battle of Midway — Historical Operations Watch
player_perspective: Composite U.S. carrier-task-force operations watch training perspective
historical_scope: Information handling and operations plotting during the 4 June carrier battle

units: Aircraft carriers: USS Enterprise (CV-6), USS Hornet (CV-8)
Heavy cruisers: USS Northampton, USS Vincennes, USS Pensacola, USS Minneapolis, USS New Orleans
Destroyers: USS Worden, USS Monaghan, USS Aylwin, USS Phelps, USS Balch, USS Conyngham, USS Benham, USS Ellet, USS Maury
Heavy cruisers: USS Astoria, USS Portland
Destroyers: USS Morris, USS Russell, USS Hammann, USS Anderson, USS Hughes
Destroyer screen: 12 destroyers (carrier striking-force screen in the cited combat narrative)

plot.note: Coordinates are for relative-direction gameplay only and are not exact historical geodetic positions.

events.headline: PBY reports Japanese ships northwest of Midway
events.detail: A patrol aircraft sighted Japanese ships northwest of Midway at 0530 and issued its sighting report at 0534. The report is useful, but it is not perfect knowledge of the entire enemy force.

events.headline: Many aircraft reported heading toward Midway
events.detail: A second PBY reported many aircraft heading toward Midway. This is an air-warning report, not a precise carrier-position solution.

events.headline: Two Japanese carriers sighted
events.detail: The same patrol aircraft sighted two Japanese carriers. The report improves the plot but still leaves uncertainty about the full Japanese carrier force.

events.headline: Midway radar detects inbound strike
events.detail: Midway radar detected the incoming Japanese strike. The defensive warning is now corroborated by a different sensor source.

events.headline: Carrier-contact information reaches carrier commanders
events.detail: Carrier-contact information reached senior U.S. commanders shortly after 0600. The simulation deliberately models the gap between observation and command-level receipt.

events.headline: Enterprise and Hornet begin launching
events.detail: Enterprise and Hornet begin launching their attack groups.

events.headline: Yorktown launches
events.detail: Yorktown begins launching its strike according to the NHHC significant-events timeline.

events.headline: U.S. carrier torpedo squadrons attack
events.detail: Enterprise and Yorktown torpedo squadrons attack. Reports arriving at the operations plot remain fragmented and should not be treated as a complete picture of the battle.

contact_update.label: Japanese carrier contact
contact_update.note: Attack reports refine the tactical picture

events.headline: Akagi, Kaga, and Soryu hit by dive bombers
events.detail: Between 1022 and 1026, Enterprise and Yorktown dive bombers attacked and hit Akagi, Kaga, and Soryu. The operations watch receives confirmation after the attack window rather than at the instant bombs strike.

contact_update.label: Japanese carrier contact
contact_update.note: Three carriers reported hit; one carrier remains a threat

events.headline: Enemy carrier threat remains
events.detail: Historical sources record that Hiryu, which escaped the morning destruction, launched a counterstrike around 1100. The player is not given omniscient launch knowledge at 1100; the scenario instead raises the unresolved-carrier threat as information develops.

contact_update.label: Japanese carrier contact
contact_update.note: Residual carrier threat inferred from continuing enemy air activity

events.headline: Japanese dive bombers attack Yorktown
events.detail: Japanese dive bombers attack Yorktown. Carrier-defense, damage-control, and reporting discipline become immediate priorities.

events.headline: Japanese torpedo planes attack Yorktown
events.detail: A second Japanese strike attacks Yorktown with torpedoes.

events.headline: Yorktown hit
events.detail: Yorktown is hit during the torpedo attack.

events.headline: Yorktown abandonment ordered
events.detail: The NHHC significant-events timeline marks Yorktown's abandonment at 1455.

events.headline: B-17s take off from Midway
events.detail: The NHHC significant-events timeline marks a B-17 launch from Midway at 1500.

events.headline: U.S. dive bombers attack Hiryu
events.detail: Historical summaries place the strike that mortally damaged Hiryu around 1700. The report reaches the simulated watch after a communications delay.

events.headline: Two B-17s attack battleship and damaged carrier
events.detail: The NHHC significant-events timeline records a two-aircraft B-17 attack at 1810.

events.headline: Six B-17s attack damaged carrier and destroyer
events.detail: The NHHC significant-events timeline records a six-aircraft B-17 attack at 1830.

decisions.title: Incoming air strike report
decisions.briefing: A patrol aircraft reports many aircraft heading toward Midway. What should an operations watchstander recommend with the information actually available?

options.label: Raise air-defense readiness; log the report as unconfirmed track data
options.rationale: Acts promptly without pretending the report is more precise than it is.

options.label: Wait for visual confirmation before warning anyone
options.rationale: Avoids a false alarm but wastes critical warning time.

options.label: Declare the enemy carrier force's exact position and strength
options.rationale: This invents information the report does not provide.

decisions.note: Decision wording/scoring is a training abstraction; it does not change canonical event timing.

decisions.title: Carrier contact reaches command
decisions.briefing: A visual report of two Japanese carriers has reached carrier commanders. The full force and exact position remain uncertain.

options.label: Update the plot, preserve uncertainty, and route the contact immediately
options.rationale: Correctly distinguishes a useful contact from perfect intelligence.

options.label: Treat the two reported carriers as the entire Japanese force
options.rationale: Overconfidence can make later reports harder to interpret.

options.label: Hold the contact until the entire force is identified
options.rationale: Withholds actionable information while waiting for certainty that may never arrive.

decisions.note: Decision wording/scoring is a training abstraction; it does not change canonical event timing.

decisions.title: Strike launch planning
decisions.briefing: Carrier-contact information is available, but weather, range, recovery, CAP, and incomplete enemy information still matter.

options.label: Support an organized strike while preserving CAP and recovery margins
options.rationale: Balances offensive action with the continuing need to defend and recover aircraft.

options.label: Commit every available aircraft and ignore defensive coverage
options.rationale: Maximizes immediate weight but creates avoidable operational risk.

options.label: Recommend no strike until the enemy force is fully mapped
options.rationale: Demands a level of certainty the battle did not provide.

decisions.note: Decision wording/scoring is a training abstraction; it does not change canonical event timing.

decisions.title: Fragmented attack reports
decisions.briefing: Torpedo attacks are underway and early strike reports are arriving. The plot is changing faster than reports can be correlated.

options.label: Time-stamp each report, correlate sources, and keep uncertain contacts marked uncertain
options.rationale: Maintains a usable common operating picture under communications delay.

options.label: Declare the entire enemy carrier force destroyed immediately
options.rationale: Premature certainty is exactly what the historical-intelligence model is designed to prevent.

options.label: Discard conflicting reports until they agree
options.rationale: Reduces clutter but can erase important evidence during a fast battle.

decisions.note: Decision wording/scoring is a training abstraction; it does not change canonical event timing.

decisions.title: Residual enemy carrier threat
decisions.briefing: Three Japanese carriers have been reported hit, yet enemy air activity continues. What should the watch assume?

options.label: Keep at least one operational enemy carrier on the threat plot until disproved
options.rationale: Matches disciplined reasoning from incomplete battle reports.

options.label: Remove all Japanese carrier threats because three were hit
options.rationale: Confuses damage reports with proof that no other carrier can strike.

options.label: Ignore all carrier reports and focus only on Midway

decisions.note: Decision wording/scoring is a training abstraction; it does not change canonical event timing.

decisions.title: Yorktown under air attack
decisions.briefing: Yorktown is under attack. The watch must support defense and damage response while keeping the wider tactical picture alive.

options.label: Prioritize CAP/damage reporting while maintaining the enemy-carrier plot
options.rationale: Handles the immediate casualty without losing operational awareness.

options.label: Stop all plotting until Yorktown's damage is fully known
options.rationale: Focuses on the casualty but sacrifices tactical awareness.

options.label: Ignore Yorktown's attack because the offensive strike is more important
options.rationale: Fails the own-force reporting and survival responsibilities of the watch.

decisions.note: Decision wording/scoring is a training abstraction; it does not change canonical event timing.
